clue.text: Sounds as if she might hold a cup for spelling

definitions.text: Sounds as if she might hold a cup for spelling

indicators.note: the clue says the word is only heard, so a spoken form stands for the written one

parts.note: a woman who holds a cup would be, jokingly, a female saucer, a saucer-ess

explanation.surface: A riddle about a woman who might hold a teacup, offered as a spelling exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' looks like orthography but means casting spells; a jokey 'saucer-ess', a female saucer holding a cup, sounds like the witch.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch casts spells, so she is the woman who stands for spelling in the magical sense.

clue.text: Use a thermos at the picnic, maybe

definitions.text: Use a thermos at the picnic, maybe

parts.words: Use a thermos at the picnic, maybe
parts.note: serving a drink from a flask in the open air: pouring while outdoors

explanation.surface: Serving a hot drink from a flask at an outdoor meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as OUT POUR: you pour while out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: To flow forth in a stream; a picnic flask is poured outdoors.

clue.text: They gather national flags, it's said

indicators.note: it's said indicates the word is heard, not written, so a soundalike is entered

parts.note: a regiment's or nation's flags are its colours

explanation.surface: Collectors of national flags, as people put it.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who select or pick out are gatherers of a chosen few.

clue.text: Uneasy about Lester being on ship

indicators.note: in a down clue being on places the first piece above the second
about tells us the name Lester is turned around into a new order

parts.note: SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A man named Lester feels uneasy aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LESTER into RESTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated and unable to settle, someone fidgety is ill at ease.

clue.text: Party displaying so much anger over a point

parts.note: so means to such a degree, so much
ire is anger
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A party where someone shows great anger over a trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening social gathering is a kind of party.

clue.text: Row about lack of writing equipment; it's ripping!

indicators.note: about shows the row wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
no means a lack of, as in no money
a pen is used for writing

explanation.surface: An argument about having no pen, which is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means a tier; 'ripping' is British slang for splendid but here means tearing open cans.
explanation.definitionFit: A can-cutting kitchen gadget literally rips open lids.

clue.text: Near a number in sorrow

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for sorrow

parts.note: misery is deep sorrow
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Close to a figure while grieving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is not close by but the old sense of stingy, tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Near in the dated sense means tight-fisted, unwilling to spend money.

clue.text: Ostracise one who made letter writing his career

parts.note: someone who does a thing as a career is a professional, a pro
a scribe writes out letters and documents

explanation.surface: Shunning a man who wrote letters for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban or outlaw someone is to exclude them, much as ostracism did.

clue.text: Master thespian portraying one in Dickensian character

indicators.note: the word one is placed inside the name of the Dickens character

parts.note: Oliver Twist is the orphan hero of a Dickens novel
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A great actor plays a role from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier was the leading British stage and film actor of his day.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier is the classic example of a master of the acting profession.

clue.text: Inventory of pigs' accommodation-or one with-it?

parts.note: a sty is the pen where pigs are kept
an inventory is a list of items

explanation.surface: A stocktaker records the contents of a pigsty, wondering if anyone there is fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser or fashion adviser is someone trendy, up to date with the latest look.

clue.text: They give enthusiastic support in the ground!

explanation.surface: Supporters cheering from the terraces of a football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a sports stadium, but the second sense is pigs rooting about in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters who cheer loudly are fans in American usage; animals that dig with their snouts burrow into the earth.

clue.text: Comfort by turning in a painful situation

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the word for comfort

parts.note: solace is comfort in distress

indicators.note: turning tells us the word for by is read backwards

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Being consoled by a change of position when things hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes REP from PER, and 'in' places it inside SOLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender spot or touchy subject causes pain whenever it is touched on.

clue.text: A clever splitting instrument

indicators.note: splitting shows the letter A cutting the word clever in two

explanation.surface: A smart tool for chopping.
explanation.walkthrough: A splits CLEVER after CLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The butcher's chopping blade is a cutting tool.

clue.text: Commonwealth party extremist looking for an evening out

explanation.surface: A radical politician hoping for a night on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Levellers were a radical faction in the English Civil War and Commonwealth period; 'evening out' is making things equal, not a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: The 17th-century radicals wanted equality of rank; one who flattens differences seeks to make things even.

clue.text: Ken takes the point

indicators.note: takes signals the first word acquiring the compass point beside it

parts.note: ken is understanding, a grasp of a subject
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A man called Ken accepts an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a man's name but is the old word for knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand an argument is to get or comprehend it, which is what one does on taking a point.

clue.text: Suitable biscuit for a 26

parts.note: 26 refers to the across entry, someone with ginger hair, so the biscuit shares that colour

explanation.surface: A cookie well matched to a particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: The 26 answer has ginger hair; a ginger-flavoured British biscuit suits them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard spiced British biscuit named for its flavour would suit someone with hair of that colour.

clue.text: Was described verbally

parts.note: the word was, described in grammatical terms as a form of a verb

explanation.surface: Something was explained in speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbally' looks like spoken aloud but means in terms of verbs: 'was' is a past form of 'be'.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical form for earlier time is how one classifies the verb form was.

clue.text: Dancer with a penetrating look, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are spoken, so their sound stands for another spelling

parts.note: a penetrating look is a stare

explanation.surface: A dancer gazing intently, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Astaire was the famous Hollywood dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the celebrated film tap and ballroom performer.

clue.text: Son of Solomon known for hav inga lot of bottle

explanation.surface: A biblical prince famous for heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Rehoboam was a king of Judah, son of Solomon; the name is also given to a very large wine bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical heir of Solomon became king of Judah; the same name is used for an outsized champagne container.

clue.text: Serviceman I join outside

indicators.note: outside shows the word for join going round the letter I

parts.note: to solder is to join metals

explanation.surface: A military man links up externally.
explanation.definitionFit: An army private is a member of the armed services.

clue.text: Animal coming in before thirty seconds

indicators.note: coming in shows the half-minute piece entering the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
thirty seconds is half a minute, and MIN is half of the word minute

explanation.surface: An animal arrives with half a minute to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thirty seconds' is half a MINute, giving MIN, which goes inside ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoat in its white winter coat is a small furry mammal.

clue.text: Islamic official of high calling

parts.note: a holy role literally involving calling out from high up a minaret

explanation.surface: A Muslim dignitary with a lofty vocation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high calling' sounds like a noble vocation; literally, this official calls the faithful to prayer from a minaret.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosque officer summons worshippers to prayer from a tower.

clue.text: Particle would turn one off

indicators.note: off says the letters of turn one are disordered

explanation.surface: A tiny particle would switch a person off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TURN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This uncharged component of an atomic nucleus is a subatomic particle.

clue.text: Acceptable character for com positing?

parts.note: a decent person, or a well-formed letter block fit for a typesetter to set

explanation.surface: Someone agreeable enough to be trusted with typesetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as personality but also means a printed letter, which compositors set from metal blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A decent person is a sound sort; clean, legible letters suit the typesetter.

clue.text: Propel theologian into an enclosure

indicators.note: into shows the theologian going inside the enclosure

parts.note: a pale is a fenced enclosure
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian

explanation.surface: Pushing a religious scholar into a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To move a canoe with a bladed oar is to drive it forward.

clue.text: Case of not being able to see the wood for the trees

definitions.text: Case of not being able to see the wood for the trees

parts.words: Case of not being able to see the wood for the trees
parts.note: the proverb about missing the big picture, read literally as being thick with trees

explanation.surface: A diagnosis of missing the overall picture through attention to detail.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is about losing perspective; the cryptic reading is simply being covered in trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means wooded or relating to trees, a literal reading of the proverb.

clue.text: On top Stalin was-or was he

definitions.text: On top Stalin was-or was he

parts.words: On top Stalin was-or was he
parts.note: Stalin was a Communist, a red, on top as leader; the clue then asks if his hair was red

explanation.surface: Was the Soviet leader on top a communist, or was he not?
explanation.walkthrough: Stalin was a 'red' (communist) at the top; read literally, he would have red on his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with ginger hair has a red top, punning on the communist leader.

clue.text: Heavy-drinking colonists carrying little weight

definitions.note: the adjective stands for the people who drink heavily, a noun

indicators.note: carrying shows the colonists holding the small weight inside them

parts.note: the Boers were Dutch settlers in South Africa
oz, an ounce, is a little weight

explanation.surface: Settlers who drink heavily yet stay light.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boers were Dutch colonists in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy drinkers are tipplers; the clue's adjective is stretched to the people it describes.

clue.text: Article you finally enlist any way

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word you
any way says the letters of enlist may be arranged however works

explanation.surface: An object you eventually sign up for, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'any way' rearranges ENLIST into TENSIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen implement is an object or item, an article in the sense of a thing.

clue.text: Job that requires looking into

parts.note: a task needing investigation, read as the very act of inspecting

explanation.surface: A task that needs investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspecting closely is exactly what such a job needs, the act of scrutiny.
